draft.title: Walks, paths and circuits
card: Walk
any route that moves along edges from vertex to vertex. A walk may use the same edge or the same vertex more than once.
Path
a walk that never repeats a vertex. For example, A-B-C-D is a path, but A-B-C-B-D is not, because B appears twice.
Circuit
a walk that starts and ends at the same vertex. A-B-C-A is a circuit.
To classify a route, list its vertices in order. Check if any vertex repeats, and check if the first and last vertices are the same.
draft.remember: A path repeats no vertex. A circuit ends where it began.

a.q: A network has the route P-Q-R-S-Q-T. Which word describes this route?
opts: A walk that is not a path
A path
A circuit
A path that is also a circuit
a.why: The route moves along edges, so it is a walk. Vertex Q appears twice, so it is not a path. It starts at P and ends at T, so it is not a circuit.
a.clue: List the vertices and look for one that repeats.

b.q: Mia cycles around her town along the route H-J-K-L-M-H. Every vertex except H is visited once. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is a circuit, because it starts and ends at H
It is a path, because no vertex except H repeats
It is a path, because it starts and ends at H
It is not a walk, because H appears twice
b.why: The route starts and ends at H, so it is a circuit. It is not a path, because H appears twice. It is still a walk, as it follows edges.
b.clue: Compare the first and last vertices, then check for repeats.

a.best: A walk that is not a path

b.best: It is a circuit, because it starts and ends at H

problems.detail: The card defines a circuit as any walk that starts and ends at the same vertex. Most Australian Standard texts define a circuit as a closed trail, which does not repeat an edge. Under the card's definition, A-B-A would count as a circuit, but it is only a closed walk. The definition matches the chapter outline, but it may teach a looser meaning than students will meet in exams. Consider adding 'without repeating an edge'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the explanations match the card. The card's definition of a circuit (any closed walk) is looser than the usual one (a closed trail with no repeated edges) and should be checked against the course textbook.

proposal.title: Walks, paths and circuits
card: Walk
any route that moves along edges from vertex to vertex. A walk may use the same edge or the same vertex more than once.
Path
a walk that never repeats a vertex. For example, A-B-C-D is a path, but A-B-C-B-D is not, because B appears twice.
Circuit
a walk that starts and ends at the same vertex without repeating an edge. A-B-C-A is a circuit. A-B-A is not, because it uses edge AB twice.

proposal.remember: A path repeats no vertex. A circuit ends where it began and repeats no edge.
